tools.name: get_lifecycle
tools.description: Where the game is: main_menu, loading or in_game, and which save is loaded. Works without a loaded colony.

tools.name: load_save
tools.description: Load a test clone from the main menu. Only saves whose file and folder both start with oni- are accepted.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: The colony at a glance: time and speed, worlds and their coordinate bounds, every duplicant (id, position, current chore, stress and what causes it, health, breath, calories, air, status, suit: the worn suit or mask with item, durability_pct, oxygen_pct and oxygen_low, or null), food and breathable gas of the world asked for (colony.world; food_days divides by duplicants_here, the duplicants on that world), power, the game's own alerts, current research, and pending blueprints and dig marks. Names can repeat; the id is the save's own and every tool that takes a duplicant accepts it. colony.food_report_kcal is the game's daily food report in the form of oxygen_report_kg: today_made, today_used (negative) and yesterday_net, in kcal. today_used_by_note and yesterday_used_by_note split used into the report's own notes (such as eaten and spoiled), largest first, as on the daily report screen. Made counts harvests and butchering, used counts meals; cooking is invisible to the game's report (neither the dish nor the edible ingredients). The cooked fields fill that gap for today's and yesterday's reports: *_cooked is the dishes' kcal (gross), *_cooked_inputs the edible kcal their ingredients used up, *_cooked_net = cooked - inputs (a Mush Bar from dirt adds all of it, a Pickled Meal from Mealwood adds nothing), *_cooked_reported what the game's report itself changed during crafts (normally 0), and *_net_with_cooking = the report's net - cooked_reported + cooked_net, the colony's real food balance for that report. yesterday_* cooked fields are null unless that whole report was counted; cooked_counted_since_cycle is when counting began (the save's load). The game opens each daily report at nightfall, not at the cycle boundary; report_day (in every report) is the open report's number, so today_* values belong to report_day. The daily reports (food_report_kcal, oxygen_report_kg, power_report_kj) and power are colony-wide, every world together.

world.description: World id from worlds[]. Default: the active world.

tools.name: get_map
tools.description: An area of the map as text, one character per cell and one grid per layer, each with its legend. The top row is the highest y; x and y are game cell coordinates and rulers are included. Unrevealed cells are '?'. Areas above 64x48 are downsampled, and cells_per_char says by how much, so omit x, y, w and h for a thumbnail of the whole world.

x.description: Left edge. Default: the world's left edge.

y.description: Bottom edge. Default: the world's bottom edge.

w.description: Width in cells. Default: to the world's right edge.

h.description: Height in cells. Default: to the world's top edge.

world.description: World id. Default: the active world.

tools.name: inspect
tools.description: One cell in detail: element, mass, temperature, germs, the room the game sees there (room: type id such as Barracks or Bedroom, name, cells, min/max bounds; type null for a plain enclosed space, room null outside any enclosure), every building there (id, operational state, the game's status lines such as missing power, stored contents, automation ports with their cells, whether a wire reaches them and the signal 1 green / 0 red, smart battery thresholds and charge) and loose items. Map features on the building layer, such as a Gravitas ruin's Teleporter Transmitter (WarpPortal), are listed too with map_feature true and an id configure accepts; find building does not list them, so take their cells from get_map.

tools.name: get_buildable
tools.description: Buildings by build category. Unlocked ones list size, placement rule, materials with what the colony has, power use or output, and pipe, power and automation ports (x, y offsets from the building's origin; logic_ports lists each input and output). Locked ones list the tech that unlocks them.

category.description: One build category, such as base, oxygen, power, food, plumbing, hvac. Default: all.

world.description: World whose stock is counted. Default: the active world.

tools.name: get_research
tools.description: Research: the current tech and queue, a missing research building if any, finished techs, and details (cost, progress, prerequisites, unlocks) of the techs that can be researched now.

scope.description: open: techs available now (default). all: the whole tree.

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: What changed since the last look: cycles, alerts raised and cleared, buildings completed and removed, duplicants lost, arrived or short of breath (with id and name), research completed, and critters the player could see that were lost (critter_lost: the object is gone, so it died or was removed; was_dying, was_marked_for_capture) or grew up (critter_grew_up: a baby replaced by an adult with a new id). A wrangled, carried or stored critter is not lost. Pass the next_since from the previous call; missed says how many events aged out.

since.description: Return events after this sequence number. Default: 0.

tools.name: build
tools.description: Place a blueprint of any unlocked building; duplicants then construct it. (x, y) is the building's origin: its bottom row, centre column, rounded left for even widths, and get_buildable's port offsets are relative to it. A refusal returns the game's reason; a place inside solid rock is allowed and is dug out first. The id returned is the blueprint's: the finished building gets a new one, reported by get_events. For wires, pipes and rails use build_path.

rotation.description: Default: Neutral. get_buildable's rotations field says what a building allows.

materials.description: One element per ingredient, in the order get_buildable lists them. Default: whichever valid element the colony has most of.

tools.name: build_path
tools.description: Lay a wire, pipe or rail along a path of neighbouring cells, or a run of ladders or tiles. To branch from an existing line, make an existing cell of that line part of the path: only a shared cell connects, so being adjacent is not enough. All or nothing: on a refusal nothing is placed.

def_id.description: A building id whose get_buildable entry has utility: true.

cells.description: [x, y] pairs, each one step up, down, left or right of the one before.

materials.description: One element per ingredient, in the order get_buildable lists them. Default: whichever valid element the colony has most of.

tools.name: dig
tools.description: Mark a rectangle for digging. Reports how many cells were marked and why others were skipped.

tools.name: deconstruct
tools.description: Mark buildings for deconstruction, by building id or by rectangle. The printing pod is protected.

id.description: Building id from inspect. Use this or x and y.

tools.name: cancel
tools.description: Remove dig marks, blueprints and deconstruction marks in a rectangle.

tools.name: set_priority
tools.description: Set the priority (1-9) of a building or errand, by id or by rectangle.

id.description: Building id from inspect. Use this or x and y.

tools.name: set_research
tools.description: Research a tech, replacing the current queue. Unfinished prerequisites are queued first, and the response shows the resulting queue.

require_ready.description: Refuse instead of queueing prerequisites. Default: false.

tools.name: set_speed
tools.description: 0 pauses; 1, 2 and 3 run the game at the three speeds. Pause before planning a complicated layout. 4 is ten times normal speed, for long unattended stretches; time_scale sets another multiple for it. Above 10 the game runs as fast as the CPU allows, which can be well under the multiple asked for, and duplicants may decide more slowly; go back to 4 or lower for careful play.

tools.name: save_checkpoint
tools.description: Save to a new checkpoint file next to the loaded save. Existing saves are never overwritten.

note.description: Why this point is worth keeping.

tools.name: list_buildings
tools.description: Finished buildings with id, position, whether they run, and the game's status lines. Wires, pipes, tiles and ladders are left out unless def or include_structural asks for them. problems_only shows what is not running, and why.

world.description: World id. Default: the active world.

tools.name: get_resources
tools.description: What the colony can reach right now: elements, food and items in kg, largest first.

world.description: World id. Default: the active world.

tools.name: find
tools.description: The nearest things of a kind, among revealed cells: an element such as Algae, a loose or stored item, a building, a harvestable plant, a revealed geyser, or a live critter in a revealed cell. Answers with up to five, and the total. A geyser lists its id (for configure study), studied, and before study study_requested and studying; once studied kg_per_cycle_active, average_kg_per_cycle (over eruptions, pauses and dormancy, the figure for a water or gas budget), eruption_cycles, pause_cycles, active_cycles, dormant_cycles, dormant_now and phase_cycles_left. A critter lists id, critter (prefab; a species query such as Squirrel or Drecko also finds its babies, SquirrelBaby finds only babies), name, wild, age_cycles, max_age_cycles, wildness_pct, happiness, capturable, marked_for_capture and room (the room type it is in).

query.description: Element, item or building id; part of a plant id. Empty lists every plant.

limit.description: How many to list, up to 100. Default: 5.

x.description: Measure from here. Default: the first duplicant on that world, else the world's middle.

world.description: World id. Default: the active world.

tools.name: get_progress
tools.description: The stage goal's numbers now and one row per cycle finished this session: duplicants, food, breathable gas, oxygen and power, and open alerts. Use it to judge trends. Each row also has world (the active world when it was taken) and duplicants_here; food_days divides by duplicants_here.

tools.name: harvest
tools.description: Have duplicants harvest the plants in a rectangle when ready, wild ones included. enable false stops that. find with kind plant locates them.

tools.name: sweep
tools.description: Mark loose items in a rectangle to be carried to storage. Needs a storage building.

tools.name: mop
tools.description: Mark shallow liquid on a floor to be mopped up. Deep liquid is reported and needs pumping.

tools.name: configure
tools.description: Set up a finished building. recipe with count queues a recipe on a fabricator such as a MicrobeMusher; count -1 repeats forever and 0 clears it. seed plants in a planter or farm tile. storage_filter sets what a storage building accepts, replacing the old list. assigned_duplicant assigns individual furniture through the game's normal assignment rules. MassageTable stress thresholds control when massage starts and stops. enabled true or false switches a building on or off through the game's errand. warp_action start or cancel drives a Teleporter Transmitter (WarpPortal) whose traveller was chosen with assigned_duplicant. request_suit true makes a suit or oxygen mask dock request and keep a suit (false: hold none; a new dock does neither until set). capture true marks a critter for wrangling (false clears it), critter_limit sets a Critter Drop-Off's limit. study true sends a duplicant to analyse a geyser (false cancels; the id comes from find kind geyser). smart_battery_low_pct and smart_battery_high_pct set a BatterySmart's automation range. inspect lists recipes, seeds, filters, assignment (kind, id, name), massage thresholds and smart battery thresholds.

id.description: Finished building id from list_buildings or inspect, a geyser id from find, or a critter id from find kind critter.

element_filter.description: Element a GasFilter or LiquidFilter picks out. The picked element leaves by the middle cell, everything else by the far end.

assigned_duplicant.description: Duplicant id from get_status as a string, or a unique living duplicant name. Shared names are refused as ambiguous_duplicant with candidate_ids. Empty string releases the assignment: public use when allowed, otherwise unassigned. Null is not accepted. Room-managed furniture cannot be individually reassigned.

massage_start_stress.description: MassageTable only: start massage at this stress percentage. Omitted retains its current value. Must be at least massage_stop_stress.

massage_stop_stress.description: MassageTable only: stop massage at this stress percentage. Omitted retains its current value. Must not exceed massage_start_stress; give both to change the range together.

crew.description: Duplicants assigned to board a rocket habitat module, each an id from get_status such as "101" or a name only one living duplicant has; a shared name is refused as ambiguous_duplicant, listing candidate_ids. An empty list releases crew.

rocket_restriction.description: Restrict grounded rocket interior access on a RocketControlStation to assigned crew only or unrestricted.

rocket_action.description: Rocket starmap command on a LaunchPad, rocket module, or RocketControlStation: select adjacent space orbit hex, trigger/cancel launch, or return to land on a LaunchPad.

smart_battery_low_pct.description: BatterySmart only: its automation output turns green (on) when the charge falls to this percentage, and stays green until it reaches smart_battery_high_pct. Omitted retains its current value. Must not exceed smart_battery_high_pct.

smart_battery_high_pct.description: BatterySmart only: its automation output turns red (off) when the charge rises to this percentage. Omitted retains its current value. Must be at least smart_battery_low_pct; give both to change the range together.

study.description: Geysers and other analysable objects: true asks for the game's analysis errand, false cancels the request. Setting what is already set changes nothing. Returns requested, not_requested or already_studied.

capture.description: Critters: true marks it for the game's Wrangle errand (needs a duplicant with the ranching skill), false clears the mark. Refused as cannot_capture when the critter cannot be wrangled. Returns marked or not_marked.

critter_limit.description: Critter Drop-Off only: how many critters its room should hold; duplicants deliver wrangled critters of the filtered species (storage_filter) until the room has this many. inspect reads critter_limit and critters_in_room.

request_suit.description: Suit Dock, Oxygen Mask Dock, Jet Suit Dock, Lead Suit Dock: true is the side screen's 'request suit', false its 'no suit'. inspect reads suit_configured, suit_requested, stored_suit and, with a suit in it, suit_oxygen_pct and suit_fully_charged.

warp_action.description: WarpPortal only, with the side screen's guards: start is refused as not_ready until the assigned duplicant waits inside (inspect warp_ready); cancel releases the assignment and is refused as cannot_cancel while warping or recharging. inspect reads warp_ready, warping and warp_recharging.

enabled.description: The Enable/Disable button of a finished building. Like the button, it queues a Toggle errand a duplicant walks over to do; the building changes when the errand is done. Result: toggle_queued, toggle_already_queued, toggle_cancelled (a queued errand away from the wanted state was cancelled), already_enabled or already_disabled. inspect reads enabled and enable_toggle_queued.

tools.name: set_chore_priority
tools.description: How much one duplicant likes a kind of work: 0 never, 5 most. A refusal lists the chore groups.

duplicant.description: Id from get_status, such as "101", or a name only one living duplicant has; a shared name is refused as ambiguous_duplicant, listing candidate_ids.

chore_group.description: Such as Dig, Build, Cook, Research, Farming, Hauling.

tools.name: set_schedule
tools.description: Replace a schedule's day. get_status shows schedules in the same form.

blocks.description: One character per block of the day: H hygiene, W work, R recreation, S sleep.

tools.name: get_skills
tools.description: Each duplicant's id, unspent skill points, what they have mastered, and what they could learn now (with whether they are interested, which affects morale).

tools.name: learn_skill
tools.description: Spend a skill point. Some work needs a skill, such as the advanced research station or digging the hardest rock.

duplicant.description: Id from get_status, such as "101", or a name only one living duplicant has; a shared name is refused as ambiguous_duplicant, listing candidate_ids.

tools.name: move_to
tools.description: The game's Move To order: the duplicant walks to the cell and waits there until it takes new work. Use it to pull a duplicant out of danger (bad air, heat, a flooding pocket) before it collapses. Refused as unreachable when the game's navigator has no path; the hint says what a target needs. An incapacitated duplicant cannot walk: another duplicant carries it to a free Triage Cot by itself. Returns from, to and navigation_cost.

duplicant.description: Id from get_status, such as "101", or a name only one living duplicant has; a shared name is refused as ambiguous_duplicant, listing candidate_ids.

tools.name: get_printables
tools.description: The printing pod's current offer: duplicants with traits, interests and attributes, and care packages. Each has an index for choose_printable. With nothing on offer, says how long until the next one. get_status shows printables_waiting.

tools.name: choose_printable
tools.description: Print one option from get_printables. Each new duplicant eats and breathes, so check food and oxygen first.

tools.name: reject_printables
tools.description: Turn down the whole offer. The pod starts counting towards the next one.

tools.name: wait
tools.description: Let the game run for up to 60 real seconds, then return what happened. Returns early when a serious alert appears or a duplicant is lost. Pass the next_since from the last get_events or wait. Time passes only if the game is not paused.

since.description: Return events after this sequence number.
